episodes.161293: A line of severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds across portions of the Missouri Ozarks.
episodes.161453: A thunderstorm developed and moved northward along the Brevard county coast producing strong wind gusts over the Intracoastal Waterway, barrier islands, and adjacent nearshore Atlantic waters.
episodes.162269: A low to mid level trough axis lifted northward across SE Georgia into the afternoon. This lifting feature combined with diurnal heating and moisture produced scattered storms.
episodes.162312: A trough of low pressure extended across the region with sea  breezes triggering numerous showers and storms over a moist and diurnally unstable airmass. Sea breeze mergers focused the higher rain chances across inland areas where locally heavy rainfall occurred.
episodes.162663: A couple of rounds of slow moving thunderstorms impacted Thomasville with significant flash flooding on both Sep 18th and Sep 19th.
episodes.162937: A line of thunderstorms moved across southeast Minnesota during the afternoon of September 20th as a cold front moved through. These storms produced a short-lived EF0 tornado across rural Olmsted County northwest of Dover that damaged some farm buildings. The storms also blew down trees in Mantorville (Dodge County) and Dodge Center (Dodge County) and a 64 mph gust occurred near Winona (Winona County).
episodes.162953: A line of thunderstorms moved across northeast Iowa during the afternoon of September 20th as a cold front pushed through the region. Some of these storms produced strong, damaging winds. Wind gusts were estimated to be around 65 mph in Charles City (Floyd County) where some tree branches were blown down. Trees were also blown down in Bassett (Chickasaw County) and a 60 mph gust occurred near Guttenberg (Clayton County).
episodes.163061: A cold front moving east across the Upper Midwest propelled a cold front through northwest Wisconsin leading to the development of a line of storms during the afternoon. These storms produced sporadic wind damage and heavy rain and training of the storms led to some minor flash flooding in spots as well. While storms were exhibiting circulation in the low levels, no tornadoes were reported.
episodes.163071: A line of storms rolled across western Wisconsin during the late afternoon and evening of September 20th ahead of a cold front. These storms produced an EF1 tornado that moved across rural areas of northern Trempealeau County. The tornado flipped a semi as it crossed State Highway 93 injuring the driver and then went on to destroy several farm outbuildings and damaged two homes south of Strum (Trempealeau County). The storms also blew down trees near Mindoro (La Crosse County), White Creek (Adams County) and Friendship (Adams County) and removed the roof off a shed west of Bloom City (Richland County).
episodes.163183: An area of rain with embedded isolated thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a low pressure area and a stationary front across western South Dakota on the evening of Sunday, September 19th. One storm produced a couple reports of severe-level hail and wind across north central South Dakota.
episodes.163242: A large band of thunderstorms developing along the southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina coast just north of a stationary front. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the coast and across the adjacent Atlantic coastal waters.
episodes.163243: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the southeast South Carolina coast in the afternoon and evening hours, producing damaging wind gusts across Beaufort County.
episodes.163244: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast in the afternoon and evening hours, producing damaging wind gusts in Chatham County.
episodes.163252: A line of thunderstorms moved through the area on the evening of September 20. Most of the damage was pretty minor, and outside of one golf ball sized hailstone, all reported hail was around quarter-sized.
episodes.163253: A line of thunderstorms moved through the area on the evening of September 20. Most of the damage was pretty minor, and outside of one golf ball sized hailstone, all reported hail was around quarter-sized.
episodes.163324: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the morning hours and continued into the evening hours on September 20th. There were multiple reports of flash flooding across the area.
episodes.163383: A severe storm in southeast Kansas dropped large hail across Neosho county.
episodes.163529: Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly moved across Northern Alabama and Southern Middle TN on the 19th and 20th. Numerous roads were closed in Lincoln County, with widespread rainfall amounts of 3-6 across much of the area. Portions of NW Madison received 6-8 over a few hours, leading to flash flooding.
episodes.163536: Thunderstorms with heavy rain resulted in an isolated instance of flash flooding in Okaloosa County.
episodes.163567: Remnants of tropical cyclone Nicholas over Louisiana promoted a humid air mass and diurnal convection that produced heavy rains over and near the southern Plateau.
episodes.163574: Amidst a prolonged wet and soggy period, another round of heavy rainfall over central Georgia triggered isolated flash flooding through the day on September 20th. Though much of the flooding occurred during the first half of the day, another localized report of flash flooding was reported late in the evening with another round of shower activity.
